task:
Custom inline rules silently miss matches when their regex can start with more than one character. A plugin does md.inline.register("word", r"foo|bar", parse_word) and registers a renderer that wraps the text in tags. Rendering "foo bar" gives

foo bar

. "bar" is never matched. The right output is

foo bar

. The parser must never assume where a custom pattern can start from the pattern text. Any registered custom rule, whatever its regex, must match everywhere its regex matches. InlineParser.register needs a new keyword-only option, start_chars, with default None. It lets a plugin declare the exhaustive set of characters a rule can start with, so that parsing stays fast. It accepts one single-character string, or an iterable of single-character strings. Both of these must work: - md.inline.register("at", r"@+", parse_at, start_chars="@") - md.inline.register("word", r"foo|bar", parse_word, start_chars={"f", "b"}), which renders "foo bar" the same as above. The method must raise ValueError for an invalid value: "", "ab", [] and ["a", "bc"] all raise. The error message is "start_chars must contain one or more single-character strings". Registering a rule name again without start_chars must drop any hint set before for that name. Rule order must still hold when rules share a start character. If rule "first" and then rule "second" both use r"@+", each with before="linebreak" and start_chars="@", then "@@" must render with the first rule:

@@

when the first rule's renderer wraps the text in tags. Everything else must keep working, including the built-in rules and plugins.
accept: PYTHONPATH=src:.bench-deps python3 -m pytest -q -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider tests -k 'not near_linear'
